card.name: Adjectives that could take -ally
card.fires_on: Adjectives or word stems such as bilateral, direct, visual, topical, express, and material, which sit before a noun. The word could take an -ly or -ally ending, but it is used without one.

modes.label: Adjective before a noun
modes.description: A plain adjective modifies the next noun, as in bilateral ties or topical antibiotic.
modes.example: it is desirable to use an appropriate<< topical>> antibiotic powder

modes.label: Stem of an adverb
modes.description: A word stem sits where an -ly adverb ending could follow, as in tac-it-ly or interpreted visually.
modes.example: endorsed tac<<it>>ly or actually by the attorney general

modes.label: Technical qualifier
modes.description: A qualifier such as in vitro or visual assessment appears in medical or technical text.
modes.example: Amlodipine In<< vitro>> data in human plasma indicate

card.writes: It suppresses endings such as -ally, -ially, and -entially, so the next word is less likely to be an adverb ending.
card.plain: It marks adjectives that could take an -ly ending but are followed by a noun or a different word instead.
